headline: NQ holds mid-range overnight as oil slides on Hormuz de-escalation; conditional risk concentrates in the PCE and Nvidia windows
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed Tuesday at 29,209.23, up 0.64%, inside a 29,077.72-29,338.77 range and roughly 130 points below the session high, so the cash session ended without holding an extreme. NQ September futures near 29,211 are about 0.2% below the prior settlement and sit mid-range within an overnight 29,096.00-29,309.75 band roughly 0.7% wide, which is the clearest available evidence that retracements are still occurring rather than failing. Asia rebounded into the European handover, with MSCI AC Asia Pacific up about 1%, KOSPI up 1.2%, the Nikkei up 0.7% and the Hang Seng up 0.8%, while US index futures were marginally lower. That mild divergence is consistent with two-sided trade rather than directional extension. Delayed cross-asset context shows ES near -0.11%, YM unchanged, VX near flat and the Treasury futures strip within 0.11%, so nothing is aligned toward a one-way impulse. VIX closed near 15.45, down about 2.5% and well below stress levels. Crude extended a third consecutive decline, with WTI near $80.4-80.8 and Brent near $86.3, down about 2.6% and roughly 8.5% on the week, after Iran and Oman resumed talks on a temporary joint navigational corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and Russian state media reported that a US-Iran ceasefire including free Hormuz navigation may be close. Investing.com noted it could not independently verify that report. The direction of the geopolitical input is therefore de-escalation, which is disinflationary and index-supportive at the margin rather than a discontinuity that would amplify Tail. Treasury yields are contained: the Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.24% and the 10-year at 4.70% on 24 August, and the 10-year traded near 4.645% in Asian hours after Tuesday's bond rally. Leadership is narrow rather than broad, which also argues against a single aligned index-level trend: megacaps were split four up and four down with a median change of 0.12%, while semiconductors were firm with NVDA up 2.19%, AMD up 4.91% and MU up 2.48%. Against that, the scheduled catalyst stack for this session is unusually dense. July core PCE, the second estimate of Q2 GDP, durable goods and personal income and spending all print together at 12:30Z, one hour before the US cash open, with consensus at 3.6% headline and 3.3% core year-on-year and rate-cut odds near 83% for the September FOMC. Nvidia then reports after the close, with the analyst call an hour later. No release outcome, earnings result or post-event price path is known at the assessment cutoff, and none is treated as observed. Consistent with the risk definitions, that combination raises Stress and keeps Confidence high without raising current Tail: the observed path is two-sided, volatility is subdued and no persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or session-extreme hold is present.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 published hourly assessments the mapped state was green apart from a five-hour yellow WATCH stretch between 09:00Z and 13:00Z on 25 August, when Tail sat at 20-21% during a trend-up phase. Tail peaked at 21% and then decayed steadily to 9-12% through the US afternoon and the overnight session, while the dominant mode moved from trend-up to mixed and then to normal. Stress held in a 45-52% band, with its highest prints in the final two hours as the day's catalyst stack came into view, and Confidence stayed in a tight 84-88% range. The series therefore describes a tape that calmed steadily while scheduled event risk accumulated ahead of it.
outlookSummary: The forward 24 hours contain two distinct scheduled clusters. The first is the 12:30Z macro block, where core PCE, the second estimate of Q2 GDP and durable goods print together; conditional Tail is modelled at 22-23% through the release and the 13:30Z US cash open, mapping to a yellow WATCH state, before easing back through the US morning. The second is the Nvidia sequence, with results expected shortly after the 20:00Z close and the analyst call at 21:00Z, where conditional Tail is modelled at 26-27% and crosses into the orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES band for 20:00-22:00 UTC, then steps down overnight. Between and after those clusters the modelled path returns toward a 12-17% baseline. All forward structure is conditional: no post-release or post-earnings price path is treated as observed, and an orderly path with visible retracements would justify faster decay than modelled here.
